records.issue_text: add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true is on an unlimited-length string column; URLs routinely exceed MySQL index prefix limits causing migration failure, and no length limit is defined on the column
records.rationale: In the migration `CreateTopicEmbeds`, `embed_url` is declared as `t.string :embed_url, null: false` with no `:limit`, which in Rails maps to a VARCHAR (typically 255 chars on MySQL), not an “unlimited-length” string/text column. The diff also doesn’t show any MySQL index-length/charset context to verify that `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true` would fail due to prefix limits.

records.issue_text: EmbedController#best will raise if the topic behind an existing TopicEmbed was deleted (TopicView.new on a stale topic_id)
disqus.thor removed the :category / -c option so existing import invocations using -c fail with an unknown-option error, and imported topics can no longer be targeted at a category
records.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor, the `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` line is removed and all logic deriving `category_id` from `options[:category]` is deleted. Thor will now treat `-c/--category` as an unknown option (breaking existing invocations), and the new import path (`TopicEmbed.import_remote(...)`) provides no way to target a category.

records.issue_text: disqus.thor discards the original created_at from the disqus export
records.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor, the importer used to pass created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]) into PostCreator. The diff replaces that with TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title]), and neither TopicEmbed.import_remote nor TopicEmbed.import/PostCreator call passes or sets created_at, so imported topics/posts will no longer preserve the original Disqus timestamp.

records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb defines feed_key but never uses it; the intended conditional/If-Modified-Since fetch was never implemented so the feed is fully re-downloaded every hour
records.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb a `feed_key` helper is defined (`def feed_key ...`) but is never referenced anywhere in the file. The actual polling implementation always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no use of `feed_key` or any conditional fetch/caching logic, so the feed will be fetched in full each run (hourly). This is a concrete, diff-grounded inefficiency/

records.issue_text: embed.js has no guard for document.getElementById('discourse-comments') returning null (throws on appendChild), and the iframe src silently breaks if discourseUrl is configured without a trailing slash
records.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js, `comments` is set via `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and then immediately used as `comments.appendChild(iframe)` with no null guard, which will throw if the element is missing.
